schemes.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme
schemes.owner: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
schemes.summary: Early-stage capital routed through approved incubators for proof of concept, prototypes, product trials, market entry and commercialisation.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Incorporated no more than 2 years before application
Technology used in the core product, service, business model, distribution model or methodology
Commercially viable and scalable idea
No more than ₹10 lakh of prior monetary support under other Central or State schemes, excluding specified non-cash support
benefits: Grant up to ₹20 lakh for proof-of-concept validation, prototype development or product trials
Up to ₹50 lakh for market entry, commercialisation or scaling through debt, convertible debentures or debt-linked instruments
apply: Create or update the Startup India profile and DPIIT recognition
Apply on the SISFS portal and select suitable approved incubators
Complete incubator evaluation, due diligence and milestone agreement
Use funds only for the approved milestones and reporting plan
schemes.availability: The startup application deadline was 31 May 2026. New applications are closed; approved disbursals continue.

schemes.name: Fund of Funds for Startups
schemes.summary: A ₹10,000 crore government fund-of-funds that commits capital to SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds, which invest in startups.
eligibility: Startups do not apply to SIDBI for direct funding
Startup should generally meet the investee criteria of a participating AIF
DPIIT recognition is the programme-level startup criterion stated by Startup India
AIFs, not startups, submit the formal scheme application to SIDBI
benefits: Equity or equity-linked investment from participating AIFs
The startup-level ticket, valuation and terms are decided by the relevant AIF
Wider access to professionally managed domestic venture capital
apply: Review SIDBI’s participating/selected AIF ecosystem
Shortlist funds whose thesis matches your sector, stage and ticket size
Approach the fund with a pitch deck, data room and investment proposal
Negotiate investment directly with the AIF; this is not a government grant
schemes.availability: Active as an investment programme. Startup access is indirect and depends on each participating AIF’s pipeline.

schemes.name: Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0
schemes.owner: DPIIT; implemented by SIDBI and other selected agencies
schemes.summary: A second ₹10,000 crore fund-of-funds launched in 2026, with emphasis on deep tech, innovative manufacturing, early-growth startups and smaller venture funds.
eligibility: Startups receive capital only from AIFs supported under FoF 2.0
DPIIT recognition is required at the startup level
Formal applicants to the scheme are eligible SEBI-registered Category I or II AIFs
Startup must independently satisfy the chosen AIF’s investment mandate and due diligence
benefits: Equity or equity-linked investment through supported AIFs
No standard startup ticket; amount and terms vary by fund
Priority windows for deep tech, manufacturing, smaller AIFs and broader sector/stage-agnostic investing
apply: Monitor SIDBI and other implementing-agency announcements for selected AIFs
Map your startup to the relevant fund thesis
Approach the AIF with fundraising materials and a due-diligence data room
Complete the AIF’s commercial investment process
schemes.availability: In force from 13 April 2026. Startup access is indirect through supported AIFs.

schemes.name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups
schemes.summary: Government guarantee cover reduces lender risk on eligible debt extended to DPIIT-recognised startups.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Not in default to a lending or investing institution
Not classified as an NPA under RBI guidelines
Eligibility must be certified by a participating member institution
The underlying loan must meet the current CGSS framework
benefits: Guarantee cover up to ₹20 crore or the outstanding eligible credit, whichever is lower
Supports transaction-based and umbrella-based cover
Can improve access to collateral-light or collateral-free startup debt; the guarantee protects the lender, not the borrower from repayment
apply: Prepare a lender-ready business plan, financial model, repayment case and DPIIT certificate
Apply through Jan Samarth or a participating bank/NBFC/AIF
Ask the lender to structure the facility under CGSS
Complete credit appraisal and lender documentation
schemes.availability: Standing scheme. Loan approval remains a commercial decision of the member institution.

schemes.name: Scheme for Facilitating Startups Intellectual Property Protection
schemes.summary: Provides empanelled IP facilitators and government-paid facilitator fees for patents, trademarks and designs.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Self-declaration that no other government scheme paid the facilitator, patent-agent or trademark-agent fee for the same application
The IP filing must follow the applicable patent, trademark or design rules
benefits: Facilitator assistance for drafting, filing, examination responses, hearings, opposition and final disposal
Facilitator professional fees are paid or reimbursed by CGPDTM
Startup generally bears statutory government filing fees
apply: Choose a facilitator from the current IP India list
Agree on the filing strategy and prepare technical/brand/design materials
File the application through the official IP system with SIPP documentation
Track prosecution and respond to examination requirements with the facilitator
schemes.availability: The official SIPP page remains live and publishes facilitator/reimbursement material. Confirm the latest extension notification before relying on fee coverage.

schemes.name: GeM Startup Runway
schemes.summary: A dedicated route for startups to list innovative products and services and sell to government buyers.
eligibility: Register as a seller or service provider on GeM
DPIIT recognition is required for startup-specific relaxations
Product or service must fit an existing GeM category or qualify as an innovative offering
Comply with category, quality, tax and fulfilment requirements applicable to the bid or listing
benefits: Access to ministries, departments, PSUs and other public buyers
Relaxations may include prior-turnover, prior-experience and EMD requirements
Dedicated visibility for innovative offerings
Ability to propose products where a standard category is unavailable, subject to GeM approval
apply: Complete entity, tax, bank and GeM seller registration
Map the offering to a category or Startup Runway route
Upload product/service specifications and required certifications
Participate in bids/reverse auctions or accept direct-order opportunities as permitted
schemes.availability: Standing marketplace route. Individual tenders and categories have their own live conditions.

schemes.name: NIDHI Seed Support Program
schemes.summary: Seed support for deserving incubatee startups, routed through eligible NIDHI STEPs and Technology Business Incubators.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
At least 3 months’ residency at the participating STEP/TBI
At least 51% shareholding by Indian promoters
Must satisfy the incubator’s call, due-diligence and committee requirements
benefits: Support for product development, testing, trials and test marketing
Mentoring, professional consultancy and IPR support
Structure and amount are decided under the current incubator call and Seed Support Management Committee
apply: Identify a listed participating NIDHI STEP/TBI
Join or maintain the required incubation residency
Apply when that incubator announces a seed-support call
Present to the incubator committee and agree to milestones/instrument terms
schemes.availability: Programme is active through participating incubators; startup application windows are local and periodic.

schemes.name: NIDHI PRAYAS 2.0
schemes.summary: Pre-incubation prototyping support for technology and deep-tech innovators through PRAYAS and Advanced PRAYAS Centres.
eligibility: Individual Indian innovator or DPIIT-recognised startup
For a startup: incorporated in India and no more than 5 years old
For a startup: annual turnover must not have exceeded ₹1 crore in any financial year
Technology-led prototype proposal within current guidelines
benefits: Up to ₹20 lakh prototype grant through a PRAYAS Centre
Up to ₹40 lakh for advanced/deep-tech prototypes through an Advanced PRAYAS Centre
Workspace, equipment access and mentoring through the implementing centre
apply: Identify the appropriate PRAYAS Centre for the technology domain
Apply to the centre’s live innovator/startup call with prototype plan, milestones and budget
Undergo technical and commercial screening
Execute milestones and submit utilisation/progress evidence
schemes.availability: PRAYAS 2.0 guidelines were current in 2026; beneficiary calls are issued by participating centres.

schemes.name: Research, Development and Innovation Scheme
schemes.owner: Department of Science and Technology / ANRF
schemes.summary: A ₹1 lakh crore financing scheme intended to catalyse private-sector R&D in strategic and high-impact technologies.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised or other eligible private company pursuing R&D-intensive technology
Must qualify under a participating Second Level Fund Manager such as an AIF, DFI, NBFC or Focused Research Organisation
Project must meet the RDI scheme and selected fund manager’s technical, financial and strategic criteria
benefits: Debt or optionally convertible debt generally calculated up to 50% of project cost
Equity/equity-linked financing generally calculated up to 50% of the relevant funding round
Long-horizon capital for R&D-heavy projects
apply: Review current ANRF RDI implementation guidelines
Identify an approved Second Level Fund Manager, such as a notified TDB route
Register and submit project, technology, IP, budget and commercialisation information
Complete technical appraisal, financial due diligence and milestone contracting
schemes.availability: Active implementation framework in 2026. Startups apply through participating second-level fund managers.

schemes.name: National Quantum Mission Startup Support
schemes.summary: Mission-backed support for quantum R&D, prototypes, products and commercialisation through four thematic hubs.
eligibility: Quantum-technology startup, preferably DPIIT-recognised
Indian ownership/control requirements may apply under each call
Proposal must fit a thematic hub: computing, communication, sensing/metrology, or materials/devices
Must satisfy the call’s novelty, feasibility, impact, team and fund-use criteria
benefits: Seed/prototype or scale-up support routed through NQM hubs
Research infrastructure, technical networks and industry-academia collaboration
No universal ticket size; each call/hub publishes its own support terms
apply: Choose the thematic hub matching the technology
Monitor DST/NQM and hub call pages
Submit the technical proposal, TRL evidence, work plan, budget, IP position and commercialisation case
Complete expert evaluation and hub contracting
schemes.availability: Mission is active; startup support is call-based through the relevant thematic hub.

schemes.name: Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups and MSMEs
schemes.owner: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
schemes.summary: Supports Indian innovators in moving from idea to working prototype, patenting and commercialisation.
eligibility: Indian citizen with an innovative idea, or eligible public-funded organisation/innovation-promoting entity
Phase II generally requires a demonstrated proof of concept or prior supported innovation
Project must be a product/process/technology innovation rather than routine business expansion
Applicant must meet the current DSIR category and cost-sharing rules
benefits: Phase I Category I: up to ₹2 lakh or 90% of project cost
Phase I Category II: up to ₹20 lakh or 90% of project cost
Phase II: up to ₹50 lakh or 50% of project cost
PRISM R&D proposal: up to ₹50 lakh, limited to 50% of cost
apply: Select the correct PRISM phase/category
Prepare problem statement, novelty search, technical plan, prototype milestones, budget and commercial path
Submit through DSIR/identified outreach centre when a call is open
Complete PASC evaluation and milestone reporting
schemes.availability: Official scheme page is current; use the active DSIR call or outreach-centre instructions.

schemes.name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant
schemes.summary: BIRAC’s flagship early-stage biotech programme for converting a scientific idea into proof of concept.
eligibility: Individual entrepreneur or eligible startup
Must be incubated in an incubator; it need not be BIRAC-supported
Proposal must be biotech or life-science led and capable of translation into a product/technology
Meet the current Indian ownership, entity-age, conflict and prior-funding conditions in the BIG call
benefits: Grant-in-aid up to ₹50 lakh for up to 18 months
Technical, IP, legal, regulatory and business mentoring
Investor, industry and peer-network access
apply: Register on the BIRAC portal
Apply during a national BIG call, typically issued at least twice yearly
Choose/confirm an eligible incubator and BIG partner
Submit technical proposal, milestones, budget, team credentials and commercialisation case
Complete expert review, presentation and contracting
schemes.availability: Periodic national calls, typically around January and July; confirm the live deadline.

schemes.name: Biotechnology Innovation Fund – Accelerating Entrepreneurs
schemes.summary: A biotech fund-of-funds that invests in SEBI-registered AIFs, which then invest in biotech and allied startups.
eligibility: Startup/SME in biotech, healthcare, life sciences, pharma, biopharma, medtech, diagnostics, industrial biotech, agritech, bio-IT or allied areas
Must meet the selected AcE daughter fund’s thesis and diligence
Formal scheme applicants are eligible Category I/II AIFs
benefits: Startup ticket up to ₹7 crore, with possible follow-on up to ₹3.5 crore under programme parameters
Equity capital plus fund-manager support
BIRAC commitment to a daughter fund is capped under the AcE guidelines
apply: Review BIRAC’s AcE fund-partner information
Identify a daughter fund whose sector/stage fits
Approach the fund with investment materials
Complete commercial due diligence and negotiate equity terms
schemes.availability: Active as a fund-routed opportunity; availability depends on participating AIFs.

schemes.name: BIRAC Incubator SEED Fund
schemes.summary: Early-stage equity or equity-linked support for biotech startups through selected BIRAC incubators.
eligibility: Biotech, medtech or life-sciences startup
Must apply through a participating incubator
Must pass incubator investment screening, valuation and due diligence
Use must match early product/company development objectives
benefits: Up to ₹30 lakh per startup as equity or equity-linked support
Incubator mentoring and investment readiness
Bridge toward angel, VC or commercial debt
apply: Find a SEED Fund partner on BIRAC’s programme page
Apply to the partner’s live startup call
Submit pitch, cap table, financials, technical milestones and proposed use of funds
Complete investment committee process and instrument documentation
schemes.availability: Applications are routed through participating incubators and their individual calls.

schemes.name: LEAP Fund – Launching Entrepreneurial Driven Affordable Products
schemes.summary: Commercialisation capital for biotech startups that have moved beyond the smaller SEED Fund ticket.
eligibility: Biotech, medtech or life-sciences startup
Funding need generally above ₹30 lakh
Must qualify through a participating BioNEST/LEAP fund partner
Product/technology should be ready for pilot or commercialisation and capable of attracting venture capital
benefits: More than ₹30 lakh and up to ₹1 crore per startup
Equity or equity-linked investment
Commercialisation, pilot and fundraising support from the partner incubator
apply: Identify the relevant LEAP fund partner
Apply during that partner’s funding window
Provide pilot evidence, regulatory/IP position, commercial plan, cap table and valuation case
Complete investment committee and transaction documentation
schemes.availability: Partner-routed; calls and sector focus vary by BioNEST/LEAP partner.

schemes.name: SPARSH – Social Innovation Programme for Products Affordable and Relevant to Social Health
schemes.summary: Supports affordable biotech and health solutions for underserved communities through product-development and immersion components.
eligibility: For startup category: Indian biotech startup generally less than 3 years old
Eligible LLP generally less than 3 years old
Academic scientists and researchers may qualify under call-specific categories
Proposal must address the announced social-health theme
benefits: Grant-in-aid up to ₹50 lakh for up to 18 months under the product-development component
Social-innovation immersion, community need discovery and mentoring
Call-specific technical and ecosystem support
apply: Monitor BIRAC’s call-for-proposals page for the thematic Letter of Intent
Submit the LoI online
If shortlisted, develop the full proposal, milestones and budget
Complete technical review and agreement
schemes.availability: Calls are thematic and generally announced periodically; check the current BIRAC CFP page.

schemes.name: AgriSURE – Agri Fund for Startups and Rural Enterprises
schemes.owner: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare / NABVENTURES
schemes.summary: A ₹750 crore blended investment fund for high-impact agriculture and rural ventures, with direct and fund-of-funds routes.
eligibility: Startup working in agriculture, allied sectors or rural development
Must satisfy NABVENTURES investment merit, governance and diligence
AIF applicants must be SEBI-registered and invest in eligible agri/rural ventures
Technology, value-chain impact and scalability are central selection considerations
benefits: Fund-of-funds corpus of ₹450 crore and direct investment corpus of ₹300 crore
Startup ticket up to ₹25 crore, subject to investment merit
Potential incubation, mentoring and ecosystem access
apply: Review AgriSURE’s investment thesis
Submit an investment approach to NABVENTURES or an eligible supported fund
Provide pitch deck, audited/management financials, cap table, impact case and data room
Complete investment committee diligence and negotiate terms
schemes.availability: Active investment programme; not a universal grant and no automatic entitlement.

schemes.name: Innovation and Agri-Entrepreneurship Programme under RKVY
schemes.owner: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
schemes.summary: Agri-startup incubation and grant support through RKVY-RAFTAAR agribusiness incubators.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup for startup funding route
Agriculture or allied-sector innovation
Must apply through the relevant R-ABI cohort and satisfy its programme criteria
Pre-seed applicants may be at ideation/validation; seed applicants need a more developed venture and milestone plan
benefits: Pre-seed support up to ₹5 lakh
Seed-stage support up to ₹25 lakh
Incubation, mentoring and sector connections
apply: Review open cohorts on the Agri Startup portal
Choose an R-ABI matching the sector/geography
Submit venture details, innovation, team, budget and milestones
Attend selection bootcamp/pitch if shortlisted
Complete incubation and milestone-based grant process
schemes.availability: Periodic calls through R-ABIs; confirm the active cohort and deadline.

schemes.name: Startup Accelerators of MeitY for Product Innovation, Development and Growth
schemes.owner: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
schemes.summary: Supports IT-product startups through selected accelerators, combining acceleration services and matched investment.
eligibility: IT-based startup selected by a SAMRIDH-supported accelerator
Startup must meet the accelerator cohort’s product, traction and scale-readiness criteria
Formal scheme applicants for accelerator support are eligible not-for-profit accelerators
Private matching investment is part of the startup funding model
benefits: Government-side investment up to ₹40 lakh, with average target around ₹30 lakh per startup per cohort
Equal matching private investment up to ₹40 lakh, subject to valuation/stage
Customer, investor, internationalisation and product-growth support
apply: Review the MeitY Startup Hub list of SAMRIDH accelerators
Apply to an accelerator’s live cohort
Complete product, traction and investment screening
Agree valuation/instrument and acceleration milestones
schemes.availability: Startup access is through selected accelerators and their periodic cohorts.

schemes.name: Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups
schemes.owner: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
sector: Tier II and Tier III cities
schemes.summary: Builds startup capacity in Tier-II and Tier-III cities through implementing agencies that provide funding, infrastructure and mentoring.
eligibility: Startup support is routed through a GENESIS Implementing Agency
Technology startup located in or serving the targeted Tier-II/Tier-III ecosystem
Must satisfy the IA’s programme and call criteria
For deep-tech support, the proposal must meet the relevant technology and milestone bar
benefits: Startup/pilot funding from about ₹10 lakh for early-stage ventures up to ₹1 crore for deep-tech startups
Mentors, innovation infrastructure and ecosystem access
Capacity-building support in smaller cities
apply: Use the MeitY Startup Hub GENESIS page to identify participating IAs and opportunities
Apply to the appropriate IA/startup call
Submit innovation, team, location, milestone and budget information
Complete IA evaluation and programme onboarding
schemes.availability: Implementing-agency applications are accepted throughout the year; startup opportunities are routed through those agencies.

schemes.name: STPI Next Generation Incubation Scheme
schemes.owner: MeitY / Software Technology Parks of India
sector: Tier II and Tier III cities
schemes.summary: Incubation, funding and mentoring for software-product and technology startups, with a focus on Tier-II/III cities.
eligibility: Indian technology/software-product startup or eligible innovator
DPIIT recognition is encouraged
Individuals, researchers, LLPs or partnerships may be required to incorporate as a private limited company if selected
Must fit the current location/challenge call
benefits: Seed/risk funding up to ₹25 lakh for selected startups
Incubation infrastructure, labs, testing and equipment
Mentoring, industry connections, marketing and product-lifecycle guidance
apply: Register on the STPI Startup Portal
Select an open NGIS/centre challenge
Submit venture, product, technology, team, market and funding plan
Pitch to the selection panel and complete incubation terms
schemes.availability: Periodic challenge and centre-specific calls.

schemes.name: Chips to Startup Programme
schemes.owner: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
schemes.access: through project calls and academic collaboration
schemes.summary: Builds semiconductor design capability through training, chip-development projects, tools and fabrication/prototyping support.
eligibility: Primary applicants are eligible academic institutions and R&D organisations
Startups and MSMEs participate through academia-industry projects, challenges, hackathons or RFPs
Proposal must relate to ASIC, SoC, FPGA, IP core, embedded-system or semiconductor-system development
Meet the specific C2S call and consortium requirements
benefits: Financial and technical support for approved chip-design projects
Access to EDA tools, IP repositories, MPW/fabrication, prototyping and post-design support
Training and ecosystem collaboration
apply: Monitor the C2S portal for an applicable call
Form the required academic/industry consortium where necessary
Submit the prescribed technical proposal, work packages, fabrication plan, team and budget
Complete technical evaluation and project agreement
schemes.availability: Call-based; many startup routes require an academic or R&D collaboration.

schemes.name: Innovations for Defence Excellence
schemes.owner: Ministry of Defence / Defence Innovation Organisation
schemes.summary: Challenge-led grants and user support for indigenous defence and aerospace solutions.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup, eligible MSME/company, or individual innovator depending on challenge
Must address a published defence problem statement or open challenge
Indian entity/ownership conditions apply under the challenge
Must accept milestone, IP, security, testing and user-evaluation conditions
benefits: Grant/support generally ranging from ₹1.5 crore to ₹10 crore depending on iDEX challenge route
Partner-incubator mentoring and infrastructure
Defence user interaction, trials and potential procurement pathway
apply: Create an account on iDEX
Choose a live DISC, Open Challenge, iDEX Prime or other published route
Submit the proposed solution, TRL, team, budget, milestones and IP position
Pitch and complete technical/user evaluation
Contract with DIO and execute milestones
schemes.availability: Periodic live challenges; eligibility and grant ceiling vary by route.

schemes.name: Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX
schemes.owner: Ministry of Defence / Defence Innovation Organisation
schemes.summary: Large-ticket iDEX sub-scheme for strategically critical defence technologies requiring substantial R&D.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup, eligible Indian company or individual innovator under the challenge
Must address an ADITI challenge in a critical technology area
Indian ownership/control and security conditions apply
Strong advanced-R&D capability, milestones and co-funding plan are expected
benefits: Grant up to 50% of product-development budget, capped at ₹25 crore per project
Partner-incubator support and defence-user engagement
Path toward trials and acquisition if successfully developed
apply: Monitor ADITI challenges on iDEX
Submit technical architecture, maturity, budget, co-funding, IP and security plan
Pass expert and user evaluation
Execute the DIO agreement and milestone reviews
schemes.availability: Periodic ADITI challenges; not continuously open for arbitrary proposals.

schemes.name: Technology Development Fund
schemes.summary: Funds Indian industry and startups to develop defence technologies against published requirements.
eligibility: Eligible Indian company, partnership, LLP, one-person company or proprietorship
For the startup route: DPIIT recognised and incubated at a Central/State-government-assisted incubator
At least 50% ownership and control by Indian citizens
Proposal must match a listed TDF requirement and meet security/technical conditions
benefits: Up to 90% funding for projects with cost up to ₹10 crore
Prototype development and trial support
DRDO/Service requirement linkage
apply: Register on the TDF portal
Select a listed project requirement
Submit technical proposal, consortium/subcontracting plan, budget, milestones and ownership documents
Undergo technical, financial and security evaluation
Execute milestone agreement
schemes.availability: Project calls are published on the TDF portal.

schemes.name: IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme
schemes.summary: Milestone grant and mentoring for early-stage space startups moving from concept toward prototype.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised early-stage startup
Innovative space-sector idea/project or space-enabled solution matching the opportunity
No more than ₹50 lakh monetary support under another Central or State scheme
Meet the cohort/theme and Indian-entity conditions
benefits: Grant of up to ₹1 crore, released against milestones
Mentoring, training and networking
IN-SPACe ecosystem access
apply: Monitor IN-SPACe announcements for a relevant Seed Fund opportunity
Register and submit startup, technology, TRL, budget and milestone information
Complete screening and presentation
Execute the grant agreement and report milestones
schemes.availability: Opportunities are announced from time to time; there is no universal always-open application.

schemes.name: Digital Communication Innovation Square
schemes.summary: Milestone grants for indigenous telecom and digital-communication products across R&D, PoC, pilot and manufacturing readiness.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup, eligible Indian MSME/company or individual innovator
For company/MSME route, Indian ownership/headquarters conditions apply
Individual innovators must form an eligible startup/MSME before agreement and fund release
Proposal must address telecom/digital-communication innovation
benefits: Startups: up to ₹50 lakh
MSMEs: up to ₹2 crore
High-funding technology products: up to ₹10 crore
Milestone-based support
apply: Register on the DCIS portal during an open call
Submit problem, novelty, design, TRL, IP, commercialisation plan, milestones and budget
Complete expert evaluation/presentation
Form the required legal entity before agreement if applying as an individual
schemes.availability: Call-based; check the portal for current proposal windows.

schemes.name: Grant for Research and Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical Textiles
schemes.owner: Ministry of Textiles / National Technical Textiles Mission
schemes.summary: Milestone grant and incubation support to convert technical-textile prototypes into market-ready products.
eligibility: Individual Indian innovator aged 21+ and incubated with an eligible incubator, or eligible startup
Startup generally no more than 5 years old, turnover below ₹100 crore and at least 51% Indian resident ownership/control
Project must fall within notified technical-textile areas
Applicant/incubator must accept the IP, milestone and monitoring terms
benefits: Normally up to ₹50 lakh grant for up to 18 months
Typical milestone release pattern 40:40:20
Additional incubator support budget under scheme norms
IP retained by innovator/startup or shared per incubator agreement
apply: Register on the NTTM GREAT portal when a call is open
Confirm an eligible incubator
Submit technical-textile problem, prototype evidence, market case, IP, budget and milestones
Complete technical and incubator evaluation
schemes.availability: Periodic NTTM calls.

schemes.name: Bharat’s Hub for Agritech, Resilience, Advancement and Incubation for Export Innovation
schemes.owner: APEDA, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
schemes.summary: Export-readiness and acceleration support for agri-food, agritech and SPS-focused innovators.
eligibility: Agri-food startup with innovative/high-value export product
Technology/service startup enabling the agri export value chain
SPS solution provider, individual researcher/innovator or solo entrepreneur under relevant route
APEDA-registered exporter or FPC may qualify
Must meet cohort-specific export and innovation criteria
benefits: Product-development, regulatory, export-readiness and market-access acceleration
Connections to APEDA, universities, technical institutions, accelerators and industry
Support across packaging, traceability, logistics, sustainability and quality assurance
apply: Review the current BHARATI cohort and “Who Can Apply” page
Submit product/solution, export-market case, compliance needs and team details
Complete screening and accelerator onboarding
Use the programme to close export, certification and market-access gaps
schemes.availability: Cohort/programme based; confirm the current intake.

schemes.name: Promotion of Research and Innovation in Mining, Minerals and Recycling Sector
schemes.summary: Prototype and pilot support for early-stage mining, minerals, metals and recycling technologies.
eligibility: Early-stage startup in mining, mineral processing, metallurgy, metals or recycling
Must demonstrate capability and intent to build a functional prototype or productise technology
Proposal must meet the current Ministry of Mines technical and milestone criteria
Incubator route may apply depending on the call
benefits: Startup grant up to ₹2 crore, milestone-based
Incubator grant up to ₹10 crore under the incubation-centre component
Support across PoC, IPR, pilot and manufacturing readiness
apply: Review the current S&T-PRISM guidelines/call
Submit startup credentials, technical proposal, prototype/TRL evidence, milestones, budget and commercial plan
Complete ministry/expert evaluation
Execute milestone and utilisation terms
schemes.availability: Call-based; use the Ministry of Mines innovation/startup notice and current guidelines.

schemes.name: NIDHI Entrepreneur in Residence
schemes.summary: A founder fellowship that provides subsistence support, workspace and mentoring while a technology business idea is developed.
eligibility: Indian citizen
Minimum 4 years of full-time undergraduate/postgraduate education, or 3-year degree/diploma plus 2 years of full-time post-qualification work experience
Promising technology business idea
Must meet the local NIDHI-TBI/Programme Executing Partner call
benefits: ₹10,000–₹30,000 per month for 12 months, extendable up to 18 months under programme rules
Co-working space
Mentoring, market and industry guidance
apply: Identify a NIDHI-TBI acting as a Programme Executing Partner
Monitor its local EIR call
Submit the prescribed founder profile and idea proposal
Pitch/interview and join the TBI if selected
schemes.availability: Periodic local calls by participating NIDHI-TBIs.

schemes.name: National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems – Technology Innovation Hubs
schemes.summary: A national network of 25 Technology Innovation Hubs that fund and support cyber-physical-systems research, products and startups.
eligibility: Startup, student, entrepreneur, researcher or other entity permitted by the relevant TIH call
Work must fit the hub’s technology vertical
Meet the call’s TRL, IP, team, location and collaboration conditions
Use of funds and deliverables are governed by the issuing hub
benefits: Financial and non-financial R&D support
Incubation, translational research, product development and commercialisation support
Ticket size and instrument vary by hub/call
apply: Map the proposal to one of the 25 TIHs
Monitor that hub’s call-for-proposals page
Submit technical plan, TRL, milestones, budget, IP and commercialisation path
Complete hub evaluation and contracting
schemes.availability: Calls are issued periodically by individual Technology Innovation Hubs.

schemes.name: NIDHI Technology Business Incubator
schemes.summary: Funds eligible institutions to establish Technology Business Incubators that support technology startups.
eligibility: Host academic, technical or R&D institution with suitable expertise and infrastructure, or eligible Indian not-for-profit entity
Clear objective of promoting research, innovation and entrepreneurship
Adequate space, governance, team and sustainability plan
Not a direct founder grant
benefits: Capital and recurring support for approved TBI establishment/operation under DST cost-sharing norms
Enables workspace, mentoring, labs and startup support
Exact approved amount is proposal-dependent
apply: Prepare the prescribed institutional proposal, governance model, space plan, budget, sector focus and sustainability case
Submit on the NIDHI portal during an institutional call
Complete expert evaluation and site/due-diligence process
schemes.availability: For host institutions; startups access benefits by joining a funded TBI.

schemes.name: NIDHI Inclusive Technology Business Incubator
schemes.summary: Supports new incubators in underserved regions and institutions where the startup ecosystem is nascent.
eligibility: Host institution must provide roughly 7,000–10,000 sq ft built-up space
Must establish a separate Section 8 company to operate the i-TBI
Long-term lease/use arrangement for the space
Capacity to accommodate at least 30 ventures/startups
Not a direct founder application
benefits: Up to ₹5 crore over 3 years for approved i-TBI
Capital infrastructure and cost-shared non-recurring support
Ignition support for prototypes/products through the incubator
apply: Host institution prepares the i-TBI proposal, space commitment, Section 8 governance and budget
Apply through the NIDHI portal during a call
Complete institutional evaluation and agreement
Startups later apply to the established i-TBI’s programmes
schemes.availability: Institution-focused periodic calls; startup benefit is indirect through the funded i-TBI.

schemes.name: NIDHI Accelerator
schemes.summary: Supports eligible incubators to run short, intensive acceleration programmes and demo days for promising startups.
eligibility: Formal applicant is a TBI funded by DST or another Central/State government
Incubator generally at least 3 years old
At least 20 startups previously incubated across multiple domains
Startups enter through the selected incubator’s cohort, not through DST directly
benefits: Up to ₹40 lakh per cohort: generally up to ₹30 lakh for the accelerator programme and up to ₹10 lakh for demo-day awards
Mentoring, networks and investor/demo-day exposure
apply: Incubators apply to DST/NIDHI under the current call
Startups monitor participating incubators and apply to a live cohort
Complete cohort selection, acceleration milestones and demo day
schemes.availability: Institution-routed; founder applications depend on accelerator cohorts.

schemes.name: NIDHI Centre of Excellence
schemes.summary: Helps a mature technology business incubator expand into a nationally significant centre of excellence with deeper facilities, programmes and investment linkages.
eligibility: Formal applicant is an established incubator or host institution
Strong operating track record, governance, startup portfolio and measurable outcomes
Detailed expansion, facilities, staffing and sustainability plan
Not a direct founder application
benefits: Institutional support can be up to ₹50 crore over about 5 years, subject to the approved call and project
Expanded infrastructure, sector facilities, mentoring, market and investment programmes
Startups benefit by entering a funded centre’s programmes
apply: Eligible institution monitors NIDHI/DST calls
Prepare institutional proposal, audited track record, expansion plan, milestones and budget
Submit and complete expert/site appraisal
Founders separately apply to programmes run by an approved CoE
schemes.availability: Institution-focused; availability depends on DST calls and individual CoE cohorts.

schemes.name: BioAngels
schemes.summary: A life-sciences angel network and investment platform connecting screened biotechnology ventures with domain investors and mentors.
eligibility: Biotechnology or life-sciences venture with a credible innovation and commercial case
Investment-ready team, evidence and business plan
Must satisfy the platform and participating investors’ diligence and transaction requirements
Investment is selective, not an entitlement or grant
benefits: Investor introductions, domain mentoring and transaction support
Potential equity investment; ticket and terms are deal-specific
Visibility within the BIRAC-supported innovation ecosystem
apply: Create or submit the venture profile through the BioAngels platform/current invitation
Provide deck, technology evidence, IP/regulatory plan, cap table and funding ask
Complete screening, presentation and investor due diligence
Negotiate investment terms directly with participating investors
schemes.availability: Platform route; deal availability, ticket and terms depend on investors.

schemes.name: Bioincubators Nurturing Entrepreneurship for Scaling Technologies
schemes.summary: Funds and networks bioincubators that give biotechnology innovators access to wet labs, shared equipment, mentoring, regulatory support and commercialisation networks.
eligibility: Formal grant applicant is an eligible host institution proposing or expanding a bioincubator
Founders and startups apply separately to individual BioNEST incubators
Venture must fit the incubator’s sector, stage, safety and facility rules
Admission and fees vary by incubator
benefits: Institutional grant is need- and scope-based under the applicable call
For startups: shared laboratories/equipment, incubation space, mentoring and ecosystem access
Some incubators run separate seed, fellowship or acceleration programmes
apply: Institutions apply to BIRAC when BioNEST calls are open
Startups identify a suitable BioNEST centre in BIRAC’s incubator network
Apply to that centre’s resident/virtual incubation process
Complete technical, biosafety, team and commercial review
schemes.availability: Startup access is through individual BioNEST centres; terms and openings vary.

schemes.name: Biotechnology Industry Partnership Programme
schemes.summary: Supports high-risk, accelerated biotechnology R&D by Indian companies, including collaborative industry–academic projects with strong commercial potential.
eligibility: Indian company/startup must meet the current BIRAC call and ownership/incorporation rules
Project must be innovative biotechnology R&D with defined milestones and commercial potential
Appropriate technical team, facilities or formal research collaborators
Applicants must disclose prior BIRAC support and avoid duplicate funding
benefits: For a company with no prior BIRAC support, grant support can be up to ₹50 lakh under the stated category
For larger projects, the playbook describes support up to 70% of eligible project cost, subject to the applicable rules
Technical monitoring and milestone-based release
apply: Monitor BIRAC’s proposal portal and BIPP calls, commonly announced in defined windows
Register the company and investigators
Submit technical proposal, work packages, budget, IP/commercialisation and collaborator documents
Complete scientific review, presentation, due diligence and funding agreement
schemes.availability: Periodic call; the live call document controls dates, cost sharing and eligibility.

schemes.name: Empowering Youth for Undertaking Value Added Innovative Translational Research
schemes.summary: Builds biotechnology entrepreneurship among students and young researchers through fellowships, research grants and pre-incubation at supported centres.
eligibility: Applicant must fit the current undergraduate/postgraduate/research fellow category at an E-YUVA centre
Biotechnology or life-sciences innovation with a proposed work plan
Founder-stage individuals are the primary beneficiaries; an incorporated startup is not always required
Centre-specific academic and residency rules apply
benefits: Monthly fellowship is typically ₹30,000–₹50,000 depending on category
Annual research support is typically ₹3–₹5 lakh
Mentoring, laboratory access, entrepreneurship training and pre-incubation
apply: Find a participating E-YUVA centre and its open cohort
Submit academic profile, innovation concept, research plan and mentor/host details
Complete centre/BIRAC selection
Undertake the approved fellowship and milestone reporting
schemes.availability: Cohort-based; exact fellowship categories and dates are centre/call-specific.

schemes.name: Students Innovations for Translation and Advancement of Research Explorations
schemes.summary: Supports student biotechnology innovations through recognition and translational grants under the GYTI-linked programme.
eligibility: Student innovator/team in the biotechnology or allied domain
Novel concept with evidence and potential for translation
Must meet the current SITARE/GYTI category and institutional endorsement rules
Startup incorporation is not necessarily required at entry
benefits: SITARE-GYTI translational grant can be up to ₹15 lakh
SITARE Appreciation support can be up to ₹1 lakh
Mentoring, recognition and exposure to BIRAC’s network
apply: Monitor BIRAC/SRISTI announcements for the current SITARE cycle
Submit the innovation, evidence, team and institutional details
Complete expert evaluation/presentation
If selected, sign the award terms and execute milestones through the designated host mechanism
schemes.availability: Periodic competition/programme; the current announcement controls categories.

schemes.name: Promoting Academic Research Conversion to Enterprise
schemes.summary: Moves biotechnology discoveries from academia toward validation and enterprise through Academic Innovation Research and Contract Research Scheme components.
eligibility: Eligible academic/research institution and investigators under the current call
Industry/startup partner required or encouraged depending on component
Novel biotechnology research with defined translation and commercialisation pathway
Appropriate IP, collaborator and institutional approvals
benefits: Academic Innovation Research project cost is generally up to ₹50 lakh
Contract Research Scheme has no single stated ceiling in the playbook and is proposal-based
Up to 100% support may be possible for approved academic components, subject to the call
apply: Monitor BIRAC’s calls, commonly issued twice yearly
Choose the AIR or CRS route
Submit scientific plan, validation milestones, IP/commercial pathway, partner documents and budget
Complete scientific review, presentation and agreement
schemes.availability: Periodic call; formal applicant and funding share depend on AIR/CRS route.

schemes.name: Small Business Innovation Research Initiative
schemes.summary: Supports early-stage, high-risk biotechnology innovation by small Indian companies, often with academic collaboration.
eligibility: Eligible Indian small business/startup under the current BIRAC rules
Innovative biotechnology R&D with technical risk and commercial potential
Qualified team and access to required facilities or collaborators
Company contribution and collaborator terms must match the approved budget
benefits: For projects up to ₹50 lakh, the playbook describes up to 100% grant support
For projects above ₹50 lakh, grant can cover ₹50 lakh plus up to 70% of the amount above it; other support may be soft loan/cost sharing under the call
Milestone-based technical and financial monitoring
apply: Register on BIRAC’s proposal portal and open call
Submit company, technical, IP, market, milestone and budget information
Complete scientific review, presentation and due diligence
Execute the funding agreement and report against milestones
schemes.availability: Periodic call; current call guidelines supersede summary funding ratios.

schemes.name: Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs 2.0
schemes.owner: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
schemes.summary: Supports ICT and emerging-technology startups through a national network of incubators offering entrepreneur-in-residence, grant and investment support.
eligibility: Technology idea/startup must fit MeitY’s current TIDE thematic areas
Apply through a supported TIDE 2.0 incubation centre
Indian team/entity and founder commitment requirements are centre-specific
No automatic entitlement; incubator selection and milestone review apply
benefits: Entrepreneur-in-residence/idea-stage support can be up to ₹4 lakh
Prototype grant can be up to ₹7 lakh
Investment support can be up to ₹40 lakh through the programme mechanism
Incubation, mentoring and market connections
apply: Identify a participating TIDE 2.0 centre and open call
Submit problem, technical approach, team, stage, milestones and budget
Pitch to the centre’s selection committee
Sign incubation/funding terms and achieve milestone releases
schemes.availability: Founder access is incubator-routed; calls and themes vary by centre.

schemes.name: Design Linked Incentive Scheme
schemes.owner: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
schemes.summary: Supports domestic semiconductor design companies, startups and MSMEs with design infrastructure and incentives tied to eligible expenditure and deployment-linked sales.
eligibility: Eligible Indian semiconductor design company/startup/MSME under the current DLI guidelines
Domestic ownership/control and qualifying design activity as prescribed
Approved semiconductor design and deployment plan
Must meet technical milestones, expenditure evidence and sales/deployment conditions
benefits: Product Design Linked Incentive: reimbursement up to 50% of eligible expenditure, capped at ₹15 crore per application
Deployment Linked Incentive: roughly 6%–4% of net sales over the prescribed years, capped at ₹30 crore
Access to design infrastructure under the scheme
apply: Review the live DLI guidelines and call on the C-DAC/India Semiconductor Mission portal
Register and submit company, design, IP, technical, financial and deployment plan
Complete appraisal and approval
Claim reimbursement/incentive with milestone, expenditure and sales evidence
schemes.availability: Call-based; exact windows, eligible costs and incentive years are governed by live guidelines.

schemes.name: Antariksh Venture Capital Fund
schemes.owner: Department of Space / IN-SPACe / SIDBI Venture Capital
schemes.summary: A dedicated space-economy venture fund intended to invest in growth-oriented Indian space companies and catalyse private capital.
eligibility: Indian space-sector company/startup aligned with the fund mandate
Technology generally at or beyond TRL 4, subject to diligence
Scalable commercial model, governance and regulatory readiness
Must pass fund manager investment, legal, technical and commercial diligence
benefits: Fund corpus is ₹1,000 crore plus an indicated ₹5 crore contribution arrangement in the playbook, commonly presented as ₹1,005 crore
Equity or convertible investment; ticket and ownership terms are transaction-specific
Strategic sector validation and co-investment potential
apply: Review the current Antariksh fund information from IN-SPACe/SIDBI Venture Capital
Submit investment materials to the fund manager when intake is open
Complete technical, market, regulatory, financial and legal diligence
Negotiate and execute investment documents
schemes.availability: Investment route; no standard grant or guaranteed ticket.

schemes.name: Space Technology Adoption Fund
schemes.summary: Supports adoption and commercialisation of Indian space technologies through approved projects by startups, MSMEs and other eligible entities.
eligibility: Indian startup/MSME or other eligible entity under the live IN-SPACe call
Project must adopt, develop or commercialise eligible space technology with measurable outcomes
Required regulatory authorisations and technical capability
Applicant co-funding is required
benefits: For startups/MSMEs, support can be up to 60% of approved project cost
Maximum support can be up to ₹25 crore per project, subject to guidelines
Milestone-based project monitoring
apply: Monitor IN-SPACe announcements for a TAF call
Submit entity, technology, use case, adoption plan, milestones, cost and co-funding evidence
Complete technical/commercial appraisal
Execute agreement and claim milestone-linked support
schemes.availability: Periodic call; current guidelines control cost share, cap and project themes.

schemes.name: Credit Guarantee Trust Fund for Micro and Small Enterprises
schemes.owner: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises / SIDBI
schemes.summary: Provides a government-backed guarantee to eligible lenders so micro and small enterprises can obtain collateral-free or reduced-collateral credit.
eligibility: Borrower must qualify as an eligible micro or small enterprise under the current scheme
Viable new or existing business and acceptable lender appraisal
Credit must be sanctioned by a registered Member Lending Institution
Exclusions, guarantee coverage and borrower contribution depend on current CGTMSE rules
benefits: Guarantee cover is available for eligible credit facilities up to the scheme ceiling; the 2026 playbook cites ₹10 crore
Coverage percentage varies by borrower category, loan size and region
Term loan and/or working capital may be covered when sanctioned by the lender
apply: Approach a CGTMSE member bank/NBFC/financial institution with the loan proposal
Complete the lender’s credit appraisal and documentation
Ask the lender to place the eligible facility under CGTMSE
Lender files the guarantee and services the loan; borrower does not obtain a cash grant from CGTMSE
schemes.availability: Rolling lender route; the lender decides credit and files the guarantee.

schemes.name: Self Reliant India Fund
schemes.owner: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises / NSIC Venture Capital Fund
schemes.summary: A fund-of-funds programme that channels growth capital to viable MSMEs through SEBI-registered daughter funds rather than investing directly in every enterprise.
eligibility: Enterprise must qualify as an MSME and meet the investing daughter fund’s thesis
Growth potential, viable business model, governance and investment readiness
No direct entitlement from the mother fund
Must pass the daughter fund’s diligence and transaction requirements
benefits: Targeted fund ecosystem of ₹50,000 crore through government anchoring and private mobilisation
Equity, quasi-equity or similar growth investment via daughter funds
Ticket, valuation and terms are decided by the investing fund
apply: Review SRI Fund information and identify participating daughter funds
Approach a relevant daughter fund with investment materials
Complete commercial, financial, legal and ESG diligence
Negotiate and close the investment with the daughter fund
schemes.availability: Indirect investment route; the mother fund does not run a universal startup application.

schemes.name: MSME Champions Scheme
schemes.owner: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
schemes.summary: An umbrella for MSME Sustainable (ZED), Competitive (Lean) and Innovative interventions covering quality, productivity, design, incubation and intellectual property support.
eligibility: Valid Udyam-registered MSME for the applicable component
Meet the chosen ZED, Lean or Innovative sub-scheme’s conditions
Provide required enterprise, production, assessment and expenditure evidence
Component-specific exclusions and cost sharing apply
benefits: ZED certification/handholding and related subsidies
Lean implementation and consultant support
Innovation components including incubation, design and IPR support
Exact caps and contribution vary by component
apply: Confirm that the relevant component and extension is live on the MSME Champions portal
Use Udyam credentials and select ZED, Lean or Innovative route
Submit component-specific assessment/proposal and documents
Complete assessment/implementation and claim reimbursement where applicable
schemes.availability: The playbook cites the 2021-22 to 2025-26 cycle; confirm post-March-2026 extension before relying on benefits.

schemes.name: International Cooperation Scheme
schemes.owner: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
schemes.summary: Supports MSME participation in international exhibitions, trade fairs, buyer–seller meets and market-development activities, generally through eligible organisations and approved events.
eligibility: Udyam-registered MSME and/or eligible implementing organisation under the chosen component
Proposed event/activity must meet the scheme and approval conditions
Prior approval may be required before expenditure
Travel, stall, freight or organiser claims need prescribed evidence
benefits: Reimbursement/support for approved international participation, delegations and market-development activities
Eligible heads and caps vary by component, enterprise category and destination
Exposure to export buyers and global markets
apply: Check the IC scheme portal for an open event/component and who must submit the application
Obtain required prior approval
Participate and preserve tickets, invoices, participation and payment evidence
Submit the claim within the prescribed timeline
schemes.availability: Event- and component-based; do not incur costs before checking prior-approval rules.

schemes.name: National SC-ST Hub
schemes.owner: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises / National Small Industries Corporation
schemes.summary: Improves the competitiveness and public-procurement participation of SC/ST-owned micro and small enterprises through finance facilitation, capacity building, market support and targeted subsidy components.
eligibility: Enterprise must meet the applicable SC/ST ownership/control condition and hold Udyam registration
Promoter caste and ownership evidence required
Chosen component may require an eligible loan, machinery purchase, vendor registration or training need
Benefits cannot be duplicated for the same expenditure
benefits: The playbook cites a 25% subsidy on eligible plant and machinery/equipment, capped at ₹25 lakh, for the relevant component
Vendor development, procurement facilitation, mentoring and capacity building
Component-specific reimbursements/support
apply: Register/verify enterprise details on the NSSH portal and Udyam
Select the relevant subsidy, training or market-access component
Submit caste, ownership, enterprise, finance and expenditure documents
Complete appraisal/verification and claim the approved component
schemes.availability: Component-dependent; confirm the live component and approval sequence before purchasing equipment.

schemes.name: Atal Tinkering Labs
schemes.summary: Establishes maker spaces in schools so students can experiment with electronics, robotics, rapid prototyping and problem solving before the startup stage.
eligibility: Formal applicant is an eligible school under the current AIM call
School must provide space, teachers, governance and long-term operational commitment
Compliance with AIM procurement, utilisation and reporting rules
Not a direct startup grant
benefits: Grant support has historically totalled up to ₹20 lakh per selected school across establishment and operations, subject to current call terms
Equipment, maker activities, challenges and mentor networks
Pipeline-building benefit for future founders
apply: School monitors AIM for an ATL selection call
Submit institutional, infrastructure, faculty and student-reach information
Complete selection and agreement
Establish and operate the lab under AIM guidelines
schemes.availability: Institution-focused; calls are periodic and founders cannot apply for cash support.

schemes.name: Atal Incubation Centres
schemes.summary: Builds world-class incubators and upgrades innovation facilities that support startups with space, mentoring, laboratories, markets and investor connections.
eligibility: Formal grant applicant is an eligible institution/consortium under the current AIM call
Dedicated governance, infrastructure, sector plan, team and sustainability model
Startups apply separately to a funded AIC’s cohort
AIC-specific selection, equity/fee and residency terms apply
benefits: The playbook cites support up to ₹5 crore for centres without sector laboratories and up to ₹10 crore for centres with specialised laboratories, subject to call terms
For startups: incubation, technical facilities, mentoring, corporate/market and investor access
apply: Institutions apply to AIM when an AIC call opens
Founders use AIM’s incubator directory to identify a relevant AIC
Apply to the AIC’s resident/virtual programme and complete screening
Execute the incubator’s agreement and milestones
schemes.availability: Founder access is through individual AICs; terms and cohort windows vary.

schemes.name: Atal Community Innovation Centres
schemes.summary: Creates innovation centres in underserved and unserved regions to support community innovators, grassroots entrepreneurs and locally relevant ventures.
eligibility: Formal applicant is an eligible institution/organisation in or serving a target region
Must demonstrate local partnerships, space, governance and co-funding/sustainability
Community innovators apply to individual funded centres
Not a universal direct cash grant to startups
benefits: The playbook cites AIM support up to ₹2.5 crore, ordinarily up to 50% of project cost, subject to the call
Community incubation, mentoring, innovation facilities and ecosystem development
Local venture and livelihood support through centre programmes
apply: Institutions monitor AIM for ACIC calls and submit a co-funded centre proposal
Innovators locate the nearest ACIC and an open programme
Submit the problem, solution, community evidence and team details
Complete centre selection and milestone process
schemes.availability: Institution- and centre-routed; current calls and centre programmes control access.

schemes.name: Established Incubator Centre Scale-up Support
schemes.summary: Helps established incubators scale capacity, facilities and programmes so they can serve more high-growth startups.
eligibility: Formal applicant is an established eligible incubator under the current AIM call
Documented operating track record, startup outcomes, governance and financial controls
Credible scale-up plan and sustainability
Not a direct founder application
benefits: The playbook cites institutional support up to ₹10 crore, subject to approved scope and call rules
Expanded incubation, facilities, programmes and ecosystem links
Startups benefit indirectly through funded incubators
apply: Incubator monitors AIM for the EIC scale-up call
Submit audited history, portfolio outcomes, governance, infrastructure and scale-up budget
Complete appraisal/due diligence
Deliver approved expansion and report outcomes
schemes.availability: Institution-focused periodic call; founders should instead apply to programmes of funded incubators.

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
schemes.owner: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
schemes.summary: Enables debt financing for post-harvest management and community farming assets, including eligible projects promoted by agri-entrepreneurs and startups.
eligibility: Eligible beneficiary category and eligible infrastructure project under current AIF guidelines
Viable project with land/lease, permissions and promoter contribution as required by lender
Loan must be appraised and sanctioned by a participating lending institution
Benefits apply only to eligible loan amount and period
benefits: Interest subvention of 3% per year on eligible loans up to ₹2 crore
Subvention available for up to 7 years including permitted moratorium
Credit-guarantee fee support/linkage may apply to eligible borrowers
Larger loans may be sanctioned, but benefit is limited to the eligible tranche
apply: Register on the AIF portal and create the project proposal
Upload entity, DPR, site, quotations, permissions and financial information
Choose/approach a participating lender
Complete lender appraisal and portal approval
Use funds for approved assets and comply with monitoring
schemes.availability: Rolling portal/lender route during scheme validity; sanction remains a lender decision.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana
schemes.owner: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
schemes.summary: Provides small business loans through participating banks, NBFCs and microfinance institutions for eligible non-corporate micro enterprises.
eligibility: Eligible income-generating microenterprise and permitted activity
Acceptable KYC, business purpose and lender credit appraisal
No grant element; borrower must repay
Lender may require business evidence, quotations, cash-flow and credit checks
benefits: Shishu: up to ₹50,000
Kishor: above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh
Tarun: above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh
Tarun Plus: above ₹10 lakh and up to ₹20 lakh for eligible prior Tarun borrowers, subject to current rules
apply: Prepare KYC, business plan/use of funds, quotations and cash-flow estimate
Approach a participating lender or use the JanSamarth route where available
Complete lender application and appraisal
Accept sanction terms and repay as scheduled
schemes.availability: Rolling lender route; pricing, security and sanction depend on lender and current policy.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
schemes.owner: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
schemes.summary: Provided bank loans for greenfield enterprises promoted by women or SC/ST entrepreneurs; retained here because it appears in the official playbook but its stated operating period ended in March 2025.
eligibility: Historical criteria: borrower at least 18 years old and a woman or SC/ST entrepreneur
Greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or eligible allied agriculture
For a non-individual entity, at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake held by eligible promoter
Borrower not in default to any bank/financial institution
benefits: Historical composite loan from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore covering term loan and working capital
Bank finance generally up to 75% of project cost, subject to convergence and promoter contribution
Handholding through the portal/ecosystem
apply: Do not assume new applications are open
Check the official portal or a scheduled commercial bank for any successor/extension
If a successor window exists, submit greenfield project, identity/category, ownership, contribution and financial documents through the bank
schemes.availability: Historical/inactive as listed: the official playbook says the scheme was operational until March 2025.

schemes.name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
schemes.access: portal plus lender or state nodal agency
schemes.summary: Supports formalisation and competitiveness of micro food-processing enterprises, producer groups and self-help groups, often aligned with the One District One Product approach.
eligibility: Eligible new/upgrading micro food-processing enterprise, FPO, cooperative or SHG under current guidelines
Project and beneficiary must satisfy state/ODOP and enterprise conditions
Credit-linked cases require lender sanction and promoter contribution
Food, land, registration and statutory compliance as applicable
benefits: Individual microenterprise: credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost, capped at ₹10 lakh
FPO/cooperative/common infrastructure components can receive 35% support under applicable rules
SHG seed capital can be up to ₹40,000 per member for eligible activities
Training and branding/marketing support
apply: Check the PMFME portal and state nodal agency for a live window
Select individual, group, common infrastructure or branding route
Prepare DPR, quotations, food licences/registrations, entity and bank documents
Submit through portal and complete district/state/lender appraisal
Claim subsidy after sanctioned implementation
schemes.availability: Programme-window and state-implementation dependent; current portal rules control new intake.

schemes.name: IFSCA FinTech Incentive Scheme
schemes.summary: Offers grants and regulatory innovation routes for eligible fintech entities working in or with India’s International Financial Services Centre ecosystem.
eligibility: Eligible domestic or foreign fintech entity/startup under the chosen incentive category
Innovation relevant to financial services in the IFSC ecosystem
Meet IFSCA registration, sandbox, authorisation or accelerator conditions for the route
No duplicate funding for the same eligible expenditure
benefits: Startup grant up to ₹15 lakh
Proof-of-concept grant up to ₹50 lakh
Sandbox grant up to ₹30 lakh
Green fintech grant up to ₹75 lakh
Accelerator grant up to ₹10 lakh
Other categories may exist under live guidelines
apply: Choose the applicable grant, sandbox or accelerator route on IFSCA’s fintech pages
Submit entity, innovation, regulatory, technical, milestone, cost and funding information
Complete eligibility and expert/regulatory assessment
Execute terms and provide utilisation/milestone evidence
schemes.availability: Periodic/category-based; live IFSCA circulars and calls govern eligibility and amounts.

schemes.name: Technology Development-cum-Incubation Centres
schemes.summary: Provides innovators and enterprises access to selected Department of Atomic Energy technologies, facilities, testing and incubation support through DAE institutions.
eligibility: Technology/startup must fit the selected DAE centre’s domain and safety/security rules
Technically credible team and development/adoption plan
Required licences, confidentiality, technology-transfer and facility agreements
Admission depends on the centre and proposed technology
benefits: Access to specialised laboratories, test beds, scientific expertise and incubation
Technology-transfer/licensing and joint development possibilities
No universal standard grant amount; terms are centre/project-specific
apply: Identify the relevant DAE constituent unit/technology and incubation contact
Submit technical concept, team, facility needs and commercial plan
Complete scientific, safety, IP and security review
Execute incubation, access or licensing agreement
schemes.availability: Centre/project-specific; contact the relevant DAE unit for current intake and terms.

schemes.name: Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme
schemes.access: through DAY-NRLM state missions and blocks
schemes.summary: A DAY-NRLM sub-programme that helps rural households establish and strengthen small non-farm enterprises through local business support and community finance.
eligibility: Beneficiary is generally a rural SHG member or household/family member in an SVEP implementation block
Proposed viable non-farm livelihood enterprise
Participation in local appraisal, training and repayment/community-fund rules
Geographic availability depends on approved blocks
benefits: Entrepreneurship orientation, business-plan support and local mentoring
Access to Community Enterprise Fund through the local institutional mechanism
Post-launch handholding and market/finance linkages
apply: Contact the Block Mission Management Unit, State Rural Livelihood Mission or local SHG federation
Confirm that the block runs SVEP
Complete orientation and business appraisal
Apply for community-fund support through the prescribed local institution
Receive ongoing CRP-EP mentoring
schemes.availability: Location-dependent; access is through DAY-NRLM institutions in approved SVEP blocks.

schemes.name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
schemes.owner: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment / IFCI Venture Capital Funds
schemes.summary: Provides concessional growth and project finance to eligible Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs through a professionally managed fund.
eligibility: Eligible SC ownership and management/control under current fund rules
The playbook states 51% SC ownership/control, maintained for at least 6 months for assistance up to ₹50 lakh and 12 months for higher assistance
Viable project, promoter contribution and acceptable diligence
Entity and activity must fall within fund guidelines
benefits: Financial assistance generally from ₹10 lakh up to ₹15 crore, depending on instrument/project
